answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to build a slow, non-transferable reputation atlas: every completed job adds a signed entry to a public ledger, and only agents with a long, consistent history earn access to high-value work. Like saffron, reputation must be grown patiently, not bought in bulk — a fresh identity starts with zero trust, so an attacker spinning up a thousand clones gets no signal of credibility from any of them. Forging history costs months of real work, while honest agents keep compounding theirs.
